rankings.passage: The annual vacation of an F-1 student who is eligible and intends to register for the subsequent academic semester shall be considered an authorized period of reduced course load during the designated summer break, provided that the student maintains valid nonimmigrant status and intends to resume a full course of study upon the commencement of the fall term.

For purposes of the full course load requirement set forth in paragraph (f)(6) of this section, no more than the equivalent of one class or three credits per session, term, semester, quarter, or trimester may be taken on-line or through distance education, unless the course of study is in an English language study program as defined in paragraph (f)(1)(i) of this section, in which case no on-line or distance education classes may be considered towards a full course load.

A designated school official may not authorize a reduced course load for a student based solely on academic difficulty with the English language, except that during the initial term, a student may be authorized to engage in less than a full course load if the student is experiencing initial difficulties with reading, writing, or speaking English, provided such reduction is recommended by the academic advisor or language instructor and the student maintains at least half-time coursework.

A student may be permitted to drop below a full course of study for initial illness or medical condition, provided that the recommendation is certified by a licensed medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, or licensed clinical psychologist, and that the aggregate period of such reduced course load shall not exceed 12 months while the student is pursuing a particular course of degree program level, and provided further that the DSO has authorized the reduced course load in SEVIS.

The student may be permitted to take less than a full course of load during the final term of the student's educational program, provided that the designated school official has previously authorized a reduced course load on this basis, and that the course or courses to be taken are the specific courses necessary for completion of the course of study.

A nonimmigrant student may be concurrently enrolled at more than one school, provided that the combined enrollment constitutes a full course of study, the designated school officials from each school involved authorize the concurrent enrollment in advance, and the school that is maintaining the student's SEVIS record is responsible for reporting and overseeing the full course of study and ensuring that the student is maintaining status.

The nonimmigrant student who is unable to complete the course of study by the date indicated on the Form I-20 may apply for an extension of stay to the designated school official prior to the program end date, provided that the student establishes to the satisfaction of the designated school official that the delay in completion is caused by compelling academic or medical reasons, such as changes in major or research topics, unexpected research problems, or documented illnesses.

The nonimmigrant student shall apply for an extension of stay on Form I-539, with the required fee, to the service center having jurisdiction over the school's location, no later than the submission of the application for program extension or prior to the expiration date listed on the student's Form I-20, provided that the student maintains a valid nonimmigrant status and establishes continuous progress toward the educational objective.

An F-1 student maintaining status on post-completion optional practical training may apply to transfer to a new school, provided that the period of authorized practical training has not expired and the student's new program of study, whether leading to a master's or doctoral degree, commences within a period not to exceed five months following the completion date of the prior program or the termination of the authorized practical training, whichever is applicable.

To effect a transfer of school, a student shall first obtain a properly completed Form I-20 from the school to which the student intends to transfer and shall notify the current school of the intent to transfer. The student shall then submit the Form I-20 to the designated school official at the transfer-in school within 15 days of program start date. The designated school official at the transfer-in school shall immediately update the student information in the electronic tracking system to reflect the school transfer, upon which the transfer is deemed completed.

A student may engage in on-campus employment, which includes work performed on the school premises and at an off-campus location which is educationally affiliated with the school, provided that such employment does not displace a United States resident and does not exceed 20 hours per week while school is in session, except during annual vacations or official school breaks.

A student granted employment authorization pursuant to paragraph (f)(9)(ii)(C) of this section may engage in off-campus employment for not more than 20 hours per week while school is in session, and on a full-time basis during annual vacations and school holidays, provided the student has maintained status and is in good standing as a student.

The district director may, in their discretion, permit an F-1 student to engage in off-campus employment subsequent to acceptance of an application for employment upon showing that the student has suffered severe economic hardship caused by unexpected circumstances beyond the control of the student, including loss of assistantship or on-campus employment without fault on the part of the student, substantial fluctuations in the exchange rate or value of the currency of the student's country, catastrophic changes in the circumstances of a source of support, or other substantial and unexpected financial hardships, provided that the employment will not interfere with the student's carrying a full course of study.

An F-1 student may apply for employment authorization with the Service for practical training directly related to the student's major area of study with an international organization within the meaning of the International Organizations Immunities Act, upon recommendation of the designated school official, pursuant to the terms and conditions specified by the Service, provided that such employment does not violate the applicable provisions of the Act and this chapter.

An eligible F-1 student may apply for post-completion practical training upon graduation or completion of course requirements for degree programs, or pre-completion practical training while school is in session or during annual vacation periods, provided that such authorization shall not exceed twenty hours per week while school is in session and may be authorized for full-time employment during the student's annual vacation and other times when school is not in session, subject to the numerical and procedural limitations set forth in this paragraph.

An F-1 student is authorized to participate in curricular practical training or post-completion practical training only after having been lawfully enrolled on a full-time basis, for at least one full academic year, at a college, university, conservatory, or seminary certified by the Service for attendance by nonimmigrant students under this paragraph, except that a student enrolled in a graduate program that requires immediate participation in practical training may be authorized for curricular practical training prior to the completion of a full academic year of study.

An eligible F-1 student may be authorized for a 12-month period of post-completion practical training pursuant to section 101(a)(15)(F) of the Act for each higher educational level of study completed, provided that the student has not previously availed themselves of practical training at the same educational level and otherwise meets the eligibility criteria set forth in this paragraph (f).

Students enrolled in a course of study at a school granted approval by the Service for language training under 8 CFR 214.3 are not eligible for practical training under paragraph (f)(10) of this section, as such language training programs are expressly excluded from authorization for optional practical training.

The science, technology, engineering, or mathematics degree referred to in paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section must be conferred by a United States educational institution that, at the time of the degree's issuance, is accredited by an accrediting body recognized by the Secretary of Education as set forth in the Department of Education's database of accredited postsecondary institutions and programs.

The employment of a student approved for an extension under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section must be directly related to the student's qualifying science, technology, engineering, or math degree, as identified on the Form I-20, Certificate of Eligibility for Nonimmigrant Student Status, and must be commensurate with the level of education the student has attained, ensuring that the employer exercises direct oversight and supervision over the student.

The student, in coordination with the employer, must ensure that the Form I-983 is updated to reflect any material changes in the terms and conditions of the STEM practical training period, including a reduction in compensation that is not tied to a proportional reduction in hours worked, by submitting a modified Form I-983 to the designated school official within ten days of the change.

No certified employer shall utilize a student granted an extension of optional practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section to displace a United States worker, including a full-time, part-time, or temporary worker, within the same area of employment and for the equivalent position, whereby such displacement causes the termination or involuntary separation of the United States worker.

The prospective F-1 student seeking authorization for post-completion practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(10)(ii) of this section is not required to apply for a separate extension of stay, provided that the student's Form I-20 has been properly endorsed by the designated school official to reflect the approved period of practical training within the parameters of the duration of status.

The designated school official must update the student's Student and Exchange Visitor Information System record to reflect the recommendation for optional practical training prior to the student filing an application for employment authorization with the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services.

Adjudication of employment authorization. The Service shall notify the student of the decision on the application for employment authorization for post-completion practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(ii) of this section in writing, and, if the application is approved, the applicant shall be issued an Employment Authorization Document bearing the period of validity.

An F-1 student who has been absent from the United States for a period exceeding five months may be readmitted to the school only if the student is properly classified under a new initial Form I-20, provided that the temporary absence abroad was for reasons related to the student's approved course of studies or authorized leave, and the designated school official has endorsed the student's SEVIS record for continued attendance.

An F-1 student returning to the United States following a temporary absence abroad during post-completion optional practical training shall present a valid passport, a valid F-1 visa endorsed with the seal of the designated school official, a Form I-20 endorsed for re-entry by the designated school official within the preceding six months, and evidence of approved practical training in the form of an employment authorization document issued by the Service.

An F-1 student who has been granted employment authorization for off-campus practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(9) of this section and who has traveled temporarily abroad may resume employment upon return to the United States, provided the student is in possession of a valid, unexpired passport, a valid F-1 visa, a properly endorsed Form I-20 with a valid certification of travel by the designated school official, and an unexpired Employment Authorization Document issued by the Service, and the period of employment authorization has not expired.

The dependent spouse of an alien classified as an F-1 student is not eligible to accept employment or engage in business in the United States, whether for compensation or without compensation, except as otherwise authorized pursuant to applicable provisions of this chapter, and any unauthorized employment shall constitute a failure to maintain status under section 241(a)(1)(C)(i) of the Act.

An alien spouse granted F-2 status may engage in study at an institution of higher education as defined in paragraph (f)(8)(ii) of this section, provided that such study is undertaken for the purpose of avocational or recreational pursuits, or is part of a full-course of study as defined in paragraph (f)(6)(i)(B) of this section, except that full-time enrollment in a degree program is prohibited unless the spouse applies for and obtains authorization for a change of status to F-1.

An F-1 student who has fallen out of status may apply for reinstatement to student status through the submission of an application on the designated form to the Service, accompanied by required documentation establishing to the satisfaction of the adjudicating officer that the violation resulted from circumstances beyond the student's control, that failure to receive reinstatement would result in extreme hardship, that the student is currently pursuing or intends to pursue a full course of study, and that the student has not engaged in unauthorized employment.

Replacement of Form I-20. If an alien student loses a Form I-20, the student shall request a replacement from the designated school official of the school currently attended. The designated school official shall issue a replacement Form I-20 only after determining that the student is properly enrolled, maintaining a full course of study, and that the previous form has been lost or destroyed. The school shall update the student system to reflect the issuance of the replacement document and report such action in the manner prescribed by the Service.

The employment authorization of an F-1 student engaging in off-campus employment pursuant to 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9) or approved training pursuant to 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10) is automatically suspended upon the certification by the Secretary of Labor to the Commissioner of Immigration and Naturalization or the Director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services that a strike or other labor dispute involving a work stoppage is in progress in the occupation at the place of employment, and that the employment of nonimmigrant students would adversely affect the wages and working conditions of U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents.

The period of authorized stay as an F-1 student and any accompanying Form I-20 employment authorization relating to post-completion practical training shall be automatically extended for an eligible F-1 student on behalf of whom a timely filing of a change of status request has been made with the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services under section 101(a)(15)(H) of the Act, provided that the student's period of practical training would otherwise expire after the filing date and prior to the adjudication of the requested change of status, and such extension shall continue until the date of the rejection, denial, or final approval of the change of status application.

Any F-1 nonimmigrant student who has properly filed an application for an extension of stay on Form I-539 in accordance with 8 CFR part 265 before the authorized period of admission has expired shall, upon the timely filing of such application, be considered to remain in a period of authorized stay pending adjudication of the application, except that employment authorization pursuant to paragraph (f)(9) of this section shall be governed by separate provisions and any unauthorized employment undertaken during the pendency of the application shall result in the immediate denial of the extension request and the termination of student status.

The designated school official shall update the student's record in the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System to reflect the resumption of a full course of study no more than 21 days after the date the student has officially resumed such studies.

The F-1 student, not engaged in post-completion optional practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(10)(ii0 of this section, shall report any change of residential address to the designated school official within 10 days of the change, in a manner prescribed by the school, and the designated school official shall update the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System within 21 days of receipt of the report.

An alien admitted to the United States as an F-1 nonimmigrant student shall be classified for the duration of status, which terminates upon the completion of the course of study, including any authorized practical training, or upon the expiration of the established program end date as indicated on the Form I-20, whichever is earlier, and no specific maximum cumulative limit of years is imposed upon such classification provided the student maintains a full course of status, makes normal progress toward completion, and otherwise complies with all applicable requirements.

An F-1 undergraduate student may change their major of study during the first year of enrollment, provided that the change is processed and updated in the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System by the designated school official prior to the expiration or completion of the current program segment, and the student maintains a full course of study as required under paragraph (f)(6) of this section.

An F-1 student who has completed a course of study for a master's degree may apply for a change of educational level to pursue a second master's degree at the same or different academic institution, provided that the student maintains valid status, obtains a new Form I-20 endorsed for the subsequent program of study prior to the completion of the 60-day grace period following the first program, and establishes that the sequential educational levels represent a legitimate progression of the student's academic objectives.

Each academic level upon which the alien is authorized to pursue a full course of study shall entitle the student to an aggregate maximum of 12 months of practical training pursuant to section 101(a)(15)(F)(i) of the Act, provided that such training is directly related to the student's major area of study and is authorized in accordance with the provisions of this paragraph.

The Form I-983 training plan must be completed and signed by both the student and the prospective employer's certifying official with signatory authority, attesting that the employer has sufficient resources and personnel to provide the structured and guided work-based learning opportunity.

The student must submit a self-evaluation of the student's progress through the training period to the designated school official of the student's school no later than 12 months after the start date of the extension and a final evaluation prior to the conclusion of the specified period of post-completion optional practical training.

A student may participate in a volunteer or unpaid position while on an extension of optional practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section, provided that the training experience is directly related to the student's qualifying science, technology, engineering, or math degree and the employer adheres to all reporting, attestation, and evaluation requirements specified herein.

The designated school official shall retain the Form I-983, Training Plan for STEM OPT Students, completed by the F-1 student and the employer, for a period of three years following the completion of the training opportunity, and shall make such form available to the Department of Homeland Security upon request.

The Department of Homeland Security is not required to provide prior notice to an employer before conducting an inspection or investigation of the workplace to ensure compliance with employment eligibility verification and student training program requirements associated with an alien student admitted under section 101(a)(15)(F) of the Act.

The employer of a nonimmigrant student granted an extension of post-completion practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section must possess a valid Employer Identification Number issued by the Internal Revenue Service and be registered in the E-Verify program prior to the commencement of such training period.

The approved employer must report to the designated school official within five working days of the termination or departure of the student, whichever comes first, whenever the student's period of authorized science, technology, engineering, and math extension terminates or the student departs prior to the expiration of the approved training period.

In the event that the approval of post-completion practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(10)(ii) of this section is granted subsequent to the requested start date indicated on the Form I-20, the authorized period of employment shall commence on the date of approval of the employment authorization document, and the end date of the authorized period of employment shall be adjusted accordingly to maintain the full duration of the authorized period, not to exceed 12 months.

In the event that an application for a extension of the period of practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section is approved subsequent to the expiration of the initial period of post-completion practical training, the authorized period of the twenty-four-month extension shall commence immediately upon the expiration of the initial post-completion practical training period, irrespective of the actual date of approval.

An eligible F-1 student seeking authorization for temporary employment for optional practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(10) of this section shall apply with the United States Citizenship and Immigration Services on the form designated by the Service, with the fee prescribed in 8 CFR 103.7(b)(1), and in accordance with the instructions on the form.

Prior to initiating the application process for post-completion employment authorization pursuant to paragraph (f)(10) of this section, an eligible F-1 student must first contact the designated school official of the school to request a recommendation for practical training and the endorsement of the Form I-20.

Upon recommendation of practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(10) of this section, the designated school official shall endorse the student's Form I-20 with the employment authorization recommendation and issue the updated form to the student, who shall then submit the appropriate application to the Service for adjudication.

An F-1 student granted an extension of post-completion optional practical training under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(C) of this section must ensure that the student's Form I-983, Training Plan for STEM OPT Students, is updated to reflect any change in the employer's name within 10 days of the change, and the student must submit the updated Form I-983 to the designated school official of the school approving the recommendation.

The F-1 student must report any termination of employment, whether voluntary or involuntary, to the designated school official within 10 days of the event, providing the employer's name and address as well as the effective date of the termination, in order to ensure the maintenance of lawful status and the proper updating of the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System.

The employment authorization granted under paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(A) of this section automatically terminates upon the date the student transitions to a new educational level or begins a new course of study at a different institution, whereupon any previously approved period of post-completion optional practical training is rendered void and unrecoverable for any subsequent application.

The eligible F-1 student may be authorized by the designated school official for pre-completion practical training in accordance with paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(A) of this section, provided that such employment does not exceed 20 hours per week while school is in session, and continues to maintain full-time registration status during the academic term prior to program completion.

Post-completion practical training pursuant to paragraph (f)(10)(ii)(O) of this section may be undertaken on a part-time basis of at least 20 hours per week, provided that the student has been authorized for such training by the Department of Homeland Security and the designated school official has updated the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System to reflect the student's employment status and arrangement.

A qualified F-1 student who has been granted a 24-month extension of post-completion practical training under this paragraph (f) based upon a qualifying science, technology, engineering, or math degree at the bachelor's, master's, or doctoral level is not eligible for a second such 24-month extension at the same educational level, notwithstanding the completion of a subsequent degree of the same or lower educational level; however, a student who subsequently completes a separate eligible doctoral degree at a higher educational level may be authorized one additional 24-month extension of post-completion practical training pursuant to the terms and conditions set forth herein.

The eligible degree upon which the science, technology, engineering, or mathematics (STEM) practical training extension is based must have been conferred within the ten years immediately preceding the date of the application for the extension, and an applicant who relies upon a previously obtained degree that was conferred more than ten years prior to the date of submission is ineligible for the requested period of additional practical training.
